compiled_state.description:
Move the GET-rotation stamp out of `bindings.json` so the file stops changing on passes with no
real change. After A1 this is what collapses the **version count** (20 of 40 sampled revisions
become byte-identical), taking the combined saving to **12.8x**. session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Why
`set_last_get` (`binding_store.py:459-464`) stamps `last_get_pass` on up to `deletion_probe_limit`
(default 20) bound-but-absent keys per pass. Measured: exactly **20 entries change per pass**. So
with A1 alone the file still changes every pass and the version count stays ~180/day; only the delta
shrinks. Losing rotation state is harmless — it just resets ordering, and the existing wrappers at
`outbound_differ.py:167-172` are already fail-open.

## Approach — compatibility first
Write the new file, read `max(new, legacy)`, and **keep writing the legacy field**. Deletion is a
separate ticket (A2-2).

`max()`, not new-then-old: under mixed versions an old binary advances the in-line field but cannot
write the new file, so a first-wins read would take the **stale** value; since rotation sorts on it
(`outbound_differ.py:607`), recently-probed keys would sort first and the rest would starve. Values
are fixed-width zero-padded (`2026-07-29T21-46-44`), so lexicographic `max()` is chronological, and
`_last_get_pass` returns `""` on absence — the lexicographic minimum — so after A2-2 `max(new, "")`
degenerates cleanly to `new`.

**Migrate in memory on load; persist only inside `save()` / the `if persist:` block**
(`reconcile.py:547-549`). Adding a file IS a write, and `__main__.py:106` `_run_reconcile_check`
("read-only") reaches `load_binding_store` at `:152`. Not an ensure unit: `run_ensures` holds the
store filesystem lock (`ensures.py:155`), disjoint from `refs/reconciler/lock`, and
`BindingStore.save()` takes no lock and is a whole-file `os.replace` — an ensure unit would introduce
a clobber race that does not exist today.

**Module-size constraint:** `outbound_differ.py` is at **exactly 800 LOC**, the locked cap. This
change must be **net-negative** there — move `_last_get_pass` (`:155-163`) and `_set_last_get`
(`:166-172`) into the new rotation module; the two call sites (`:607`, `:704`) are one-for-one
substitutions.

**Staging:** add `get_rotation.json` to `reconcile_helpers.py:206`'s `_rel_files` AND the basename
check at `:227-230`, or it is never committed **locally** (GHA's `git add -A` would mask the
omission). `.gitattributes` is a glob (`.bridge_state/* merge=ours`) so the new file is covered.
Update `push.py:76`'s docstring, which names the regenerable files explicitly.

## Rollback
Reverting is safe: readers fall back to the in-line field, which this change never stops writing, so
rotation order survives and the orphaned file is inert.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The byte-identical/no-commit assertion from A1 **still holds when <=20 absent-key GETs occur in
      a pass**. Tier: **integration** in a real temporary git repo.
- [ ] `get_rotation.json` is **staged and committed locally** (asserted in a real temporary git repo,
      since GHA's `git add -A` would mask a staging omission). Tier: **integration**.
- [ ] Rotation order after an **interleaved old-binary/new-binary pass sequence** matches the
      all-new sequence. Tier: **integration**. This is the RED case for the `max()` rule — a
      first-wins read fails it.
- [ ] A legacy store with in-line stamps only yields identical rotation order. Tier: **unit**.
- [ ] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical
      (`git status --porcelain` empty). Tier: **CLI subprocess** + worktree assertion.
- [ ] `wc -l src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` is **<=800**. Verify: the
      module-size gate in `_build-and-test.yml` passes.

## Files
`binding_store.py`, new rotation module under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`,
`outbound_differ.py`, `reconcile_helpers.py`, `_store/push.py` (docstring), tests

Scope: M. Depends on A1.
